// diagnostic

E0747

This callback uses the effect `{effect_name}`, which the parameter doesn't allow.

What

This callback uses the effect `{effect_name}`, which the parameter doesn't allow.

Why

A `fn(…) -[]>` parameter demands a pure callback, and a `fn(…) -[E]>` parameter bounds the callback to the listed effects; the actual callback's inferred effects must be a subset. The bound is checked at the call site, so an impure callback is rejected before it runs.

Fix

Pass a callback within the bound (a `fn … -[]>` for a pure parameter), or widen the parameter's effect bound.

Worked example

First UI snapshot mentioning E0747: tests/ui/cffi_callback_effect.stderr.

Error [jet.NonCAbiType]: `fn(I32) -[]> I32` is not a C-compatible type for a foreign function parameter or return.
  --> tests/ui/cffi_callback_effect.jet:12:26
    |
 12 | run: fn() { print(c.call(impure, 1)) }
    |                          ^^^^^^
 Why: `#Import` / `#Export` functions must use types with a stable C ABI at the edge.
 Fix: Use scalars, `String`, or a struct with C layout; pointers only through the gated tier.
More: jet-lang.dev/e/E3203

Error [jet.CallbackEffectBoundExceeded]: This callback uses the effect `IO`, which the parameter doesn't allow
  --> tests/ui/cffi_callback_effect.jet:12:26
    |
 12 | run: fn() { print(c.call(impure, 1)) }
    |                          ^^^^^^
 Why: The parameter is `fn(…) -[]>`, so the callback must be pure; `IO` is outside that bound
 Fix: Pass a `fn(…) -[]>` callback (or a lambda that uses no effects), or widen the parameter's bound
 Denial: invocation
More: jet-lang.dev/e/E0747
